name: JNK India Ltd
tagline: Small-cap fired-heater / reformer maker riding the refinery capex upcycle with a ~Rs 1,801 Cr order book, but capital efficiency (ROCE ~17%) and cash conversion are far weaker than first assumed, and a rich ~32x multiple already prices in unwon catalysts
business_overview: JNK India (incorporated 2010) designs, manufactures, installs and commissions process-fired heaters, reformers and cracking furnaces for oil & gas refineries, petrochemical, fertiliser and steel customers. It has a strategic collaboration with Korean promoter JNK Global, which routes a large and growing share of export/EPC orders on a back-to-back basis. Newer avenues: green hydrogen and sustainable aviation fuel via the JNK Chemdist JV (still loss-making), plus a push into non-heating equipment for metals & minerals, offshore and renewables.
fundamentals_table: ~17.5% / ~12.1% (FY26) - down sharply from 46-54% in FY22-FY23; the earlier ~53% figure was a pre-scale number, not current
Rs 819-838 Cr FY26 (+68-72% YoY vs ~Rs 477 Cr FY25, which was itself flat vs FY24); Q1 FY27 consolidated Rs 186 Cr (+80.6%, off a very soft base)
FY26 PAT ~Rs 65 Cr (+115%); FY26 EBITDA margin ~11%. Q1 FY27 EBITDA Rs 21.9 Cr (11.8% margin vs 7%), PAT Rs 9.6 Cr (8.5x off Rs 1.1 Cr base). Standalone Q1 EBITDA margin ~14%

~Rs 1,801 Cr order book (Jun-26, ~2.2x FY26 revenue); >Rs 6,000 Cr bid pipeline (Rs 3,000 Cr export heating @ 20-25% hit rate + Rs 3,000 Cr domestic non-heating @ 10-12%); expected inflow Rs 1,200-1,500 Cr/yr
Operating cash flow negative/breakeven three years running (FY24 -Rs 10 Cr, FY25 -Rs 65 Cr, FY26 -Rs 2 Cr); working-capital days ~157; debtor days improved 261 -> 139
~67.8% (stable, no pledge disclosed); total debt ~Rs 91 Cr; dividend payout ~3.5%
fundamentals_narrative: JNK India has a genuine revenue inflection - FY26 revenue up ~70% and Q1 FY27 up ~81% (though off a soft comparator), on the back of the Indian refinery/petrochem capex upcycle (BPCL Bina, Reliance, HPCL). The order book of ~Rs 1,801 Cr gives roughly two years of visibility. But the deep read materially revises the quality picture the earlier note painted: ROCE is ~17% and ROE ~12% (not the 45-53% previously stated - that was a FY22-23 pre-scale figure), operating cash flow has been negative or breakeven for three straight years on a working-capital-heavy EPC-style model, and the JNK Chemdist green-hydrogen JV is still running an operating loss. FY27 guidance has also been walked back to ~20-25% revenue growth (12-14% EBITDA margin) from the wider range cited earlier. At ~32x trailing the stock already embeds Dangote Phase 2 and non-heating diversification wins that are not yet in hand.
technical_read: Not pulled this pass -- assessment rests on fundamentals + order-book trajectory. Stock ~Rs 431; ran hard in 2026 on order wins.
sentiment_summary: Positive and building. The thread (22 posts read of 26) tracks a steady stream of order wins: BPCL Bina (~Rs 1,050 Cr received via JNK Global + more pending), first US order via KBR, first HPCL Mumbai process-plant order, Adani, Middle East waste-gas projects, and a Chemdist green-hydrogen/SAF pipeline. The Aug-2026 read-through from JNK Global winning a Rs 1,713 Cr Nigeria/Dangote heater package strengthens the case that JNK India participates in Dangote Refinery Phase 2 (estimated Rs 2,000-2,500 Cr TAM). Bears on the thread flag related-party dependence on JNK Global as the contracting customer/intermediary, a cancelled ~Rs 200 Cr ADNOC TA'ZIZ incinerator order (June 2026, licensor-approval failure), and sanctions exposure from Russia/US end-markets.
community_signal: Satishwe (trusted, elevated) is a sustained bullish tracker -- 'good numbers, bidding pipeline healthy' (Aug 2026) and '30-35% topline growth for FY27 without counting new orders' (June 2026). kartik_bhat and sougataG (both elevated) also engage constructively. No red-flag concerns raised. Note the trusted-user growth expectation (30-35%) now sits above management's own reaffirmed FY27 guide of 20-25%.

bse_notes: Key governance watch-item is the related-party relationship with Korean promoter JNK Global, which routes a large and growing share of orders on a back-to-back basis (~Rs 1,050 Cr received; BPCL Bina, Petronas Pengerang, ISL, USA projects). The JNK Global cooperation agreement has not yet been formally renewed (management expects continuation on same terms), and JNK Global reportedly has internal board disputes. ADNOC TA'ZIZ export order cancelled June 2026 over process-licensor technical approval - management calls it 'exceptional and rare', no material cash loss as it was early-stage. No SEBI action, no pledge.
bull_case: Genuine revenue inflection - FY26 +~70%, Q1 FY27 +81% - driven by the Indian refinery/petrochem capex upcycle
Order book ~Rs 1,801 Cr (~2.2x FY26 revenue) plus a >Rs 6,000 Cr bid pipeline; expected inflow Rs 1,200-1,500 Cr/yr
Margin recovering: consolidated EBITDA margin 11.8% in Q1 FY27 (vs 7%), standalone ~14%; guidance 12-14% for FY27
Working capital improving - debtor days down from 261 to 139, inventory days normalised
Optionality from Dangote Phase 2 (Rs 2,000-2,500 Cr TAM, repeat-order candidate), non-heating diversification (target 40% of revenue in 3-5 years), and green-H2/SAF via Chemdist
bear_case: Capital efficiency is far lower than first assumed - ROCE ~17%, ROE ~12% (FY26), not the 45-53% in the earlier note; that was a pre-scale FY22-23 figure
Operating cash flow negative or breakeven for three straight years (FY24 -Rs 10 Cr, FY25 -Rs 65 Cr, FY26 -Rs 2 Cr) on a working-capital-heavy model
~32x trailing P/E on a 12% ROE, lumpy, cash-poor EPC-style business already prices in unwon catalysts (Dangote 2, non-heating)
FY27 guidance walked back to ~20-25% revenue growth from the wider range previously cited; trusted-user 30-35% expectation now above management's own guide
Rising, un-renewed related-party dependence on promoter JNK Global for export/EPC order flow; JNK Global has internal board disputes
ADNOC TA'ZIZ cancellation shows real process-licensor qualification risk in exports; revenue recognition is milestone-based and H2-weighted (60-65%)
JNK Chemdist JV still loss-making (Rs 3.6 Cr operating loss in Q1 FY27); breakeven only targeted by FY27-end
verdict_headline: A real refinery-capex growth story, but meaningfully lower quality than first assumed (ROCE ~17%, negative operating cash flow) and richly priced at ~32x - conviction cut to Medium, thesis fit to neither
verdict_reasoning: The revenue inflection and Rs 1,801 Cr order book are genuine, and the India refinery/petrochem capex upcycle is a concrete tailwind - this keeps conviction at Medium rather than lower

But the deep read reappraises capital efficiency sharply downward (ROCE ~17% / ROE ~12%, not 45-53%), confirms three years of negative-to-breakeven operating cash flow, a loss-making Chemdist JV, FY27 guidance walked back to 20-25%, and a rising un-renewed related-party dependence on JNK Global - Medium-High is no longer supportable

Thesis fit moved to 'neither': a realistic base case is a 2-4x over several years if execution holds and Dangote Phase 2 lands; a true 10x-in-2-3-years is not credible for a 12%-ROE, cash-poor business guiding ~20-25% growth at a ~32x multiple
No red-flag tier - the JNK Global relationship and RPTs are disclosed, not SEBI action, and there is no pledge or going-concern issue

Can the non-heating segments reach ~40% of revenue, and at what margin, given no execution track record there?
